markets.name: United States
markets.notes: In the US (and Canada) the third-generation Hilux was never badged Hilux: it was the 'Toyota Truck' or 'Toyota Pickup' (brochures say Toyota Truck; buyers and listings say 'Toyota Pickup', often with the trim 'SR5'). It was sold as model years 1979-1983; the redesign built from August 1983 was sold as MY1984 and is the next generation (RN5x/RN6x codes), so a US MY1984 is never third generation. Toyota USA's own newsroom files 1979-83 as the 'Fourth (4th) Generation' Toyota Truck because US numbering counts earlier Stout/Hilux models differently; LC Engineering calls it the '2nd generation' Pickup. Engines: 20R 2.2L for 1979-80, 22R 2.4L for 1981-83; a 2.2L L diesel (LN codes, out of scope) arrived for 1981/82. Chassis codes follow a clean pattern: 3x = short (standard) bed on the 2585 mm wheelbase, 4x = long bed on the 2800 mm wheelbase; last digit 2/7 = 20R 2WD/4WD, 4/8 = 22R 2WD/4WD. The 12R and 18R were never sold in the US. 4WD arrived for 1979 (US sources say January 1979, before the Japanese October 1979 launch), with a solid front axle and Land Cruiser-derived transfer case. Trim names seen in listings: Standard, Deluxe, SR5 (Sport Rally 5-speed package, 5-speed and bucket seats), 'Sport Truck' (the short-bed SR5 in 1979-80 brochures), 'Long Bed', 1983 'Mojave' special edition (RN44). No extended cab existed: the Xtracab arrived with the MY1984 redesign. Colour swatch hex values are approximations; codes are US-market factory codes.
unresolved: 4WD start: US sources (YotaTech, Wikipedia) date RN37 from January 1979, while Toyota Japan dates the first Hilux 4WD to October 1979; possibly North America got 4WD first, not reconciled
LC Engineering lists 22R-EC (EFI) against 1981-83 RN34/RN44; other sources put the first fuel-injected 22R-E in the MY1984 redesign. Treated as 22R carburetted only for 1981-83
Whether a 1-ton / cab-and-chassis long-bed variant (used under Sunrader/Chinook-style campers) carried a distinct code or was an RN42/RN44 with a different suffix is unconfirmed
Canada was not researched separately; assumed to mirror US codes

markets.name: United Kingdom
markets.notes: Sold as the Toyota Hilux (period badging 'Hi-Lux') pick-up, right-hand drive, from 1979 to late 1983. Petrol UK trucks were the 1.6 (12R, RN30 short / RN40 long wheelbase, 2WD) and the 2.0 four-wheel drive (18R, RN46 long wheelbase per WheelsAge UK-spec; the 4WD launched in the UK in 1979 and quickly became the best-selling version). A 2.2 L diesel (LN codes) followed and is out of scope. Only single cabs were sold; no Xtracab or double cab is documented for the UK third generation. The owner's reference truck (1980 RN30, 12R, 2WD, single cab, short bed) is the base UK model. UK listings use registration year, so a late-registered 1984 ('A'-prefix) truck can still be a third-generation RN30/RN46 from runout stock; check the code or the round-headlight body. Many RN30s now in the UK are later imports from Thailand (Siam Imports), which were 12R RN30s built for the Thai market.
unresolved: UK engine output: European TecDoc catalogues give the 12R as 67 hp (49 kW) and the 18R 4WD as 88 hp (65 kW); Japanese-spec 12R-J is quoted at 80 PS. No UK brochure figure found
Whether a 2WD 2.0 (RN31/RN41) was officially sold in the UK is unconfirmed; megazip lists RN41L for Europe (left-hand drive), not a UK RHD frame

Whether UK 4WD was ever the short-wheelbase RN36: Megazip lists an RN36R (RHD) frame for the Europe region 1979-81, and a UK-restored June 1980 4WD appears in Toyota UK's magazine without its code; WheelsAge labels the UK-spec 4WD RN46
UK colour charts for the 1979-83 Hilux not found
UK dimensions and kerb weight not found in a UK source; figures below are Australian-published RN30 figures on the same body

markets.notes: Sold as the Toyota HiLux (listings use 'Hilux', 'HiLux', 'Hi-Lux'), late 1978/1979 to late 1983, as single-cab utes (wellside 'tub') and cab-chassis (tray), with a dual cab added for 1982. markets.name: Japan
markets.notes: ハイラックス (Hilux) 3代目, the 30/40系 (N30/N40). Launched 1 September 1978 with the 'HILUX CALIFORNIA - Made in Japan, American Spirit' theme; three standard-body and four long-body variants; the top Super Deluxe had a cab 90 mm longer than standard (a longer single cab, not an extended/Xtracab body with rear space or jump seats). Home-market petrol engine was the 1.6 12R-J only for 2WD (the 20R/22R were export), with the 2.0 18R-J for the 4WD from October 1979. L diesel from December 1979 (out of scope). Double cab (ダブルキャブ) from October 1981. The 4th generation launched in November 1983, but the 2WD N30/N40 continued as the budget 'Popular Series' (ポピュラーシリーズ) with 12R-J until September 1988, so a Japanese RN35/RN45 dated 1984-1988 is still a third-generation body. Japanese code suffixes (from the EPC): 30 = standard body, 40 = long body; 12R-J went RN30/40 (Aug 1978-Dec 1979) -> RN33/43 (Dec 1979-Oct 1981) -> RN35/45 (Oct 1981-1988).
unresolved: Home-market dimensions and weights: the Toyota 75-year spec table exists but its figures did not surface in snippets

Double cab petrol code: RN45-JDP is the likeliest (P suffix) but not confirmed

markets.name: Thailand
markets.notes: In Thailand the third generation was the 'Hilux Super Star' (ไฮลักซ์ ซูเปอร์สตาร์), universally nicknamed 'ม้ากระโดด' (jumping horse). Toyota Motor Thailand has built Hilux at Samrong since the RN10. Thai trucks were 12R 1.6 petrol only, RN30 short bed ('4 ขอ', four rope hooks) and RN40 long bed ('5 ขอ'); diesel LN30/LN40 also existed (out of scope). Thai RN30s are exported to the UK today (e.g. Siam Imports), so a UK listing of a Thai-origin RN30 is a genuine match for the owner's truck.
